n: The great speeches are ending. Moses now turns to the transfer of leadership and final arrangements before his departure.
At 120, Moses says he can no longer lead in daily affairs, and God has told him he will not cross the Jordan.

f.w: an hundred and twenty years old

f.g: Lead the people in their activities, including battle.

f.w: Thou shalt not go over this Jordan

n: The real leader is the Lord — he will go before them. Joshua will lead as his servant. Leadership changes, but God remains.

f.w: Joshua, he shall go over before thee

n: God will defeat the Canaanites just as he defeated Sihon and Og.
The Lord will hand over the enemy; Israel must then carry out his commands concerning them.
Moses’ encouragement to all Israel: be strong, be brave, don’t fear. God will never fail or abandon you. Hebrews quotes this promise to Christians.

f.w: he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee
Be strong and of a good courage

n: Moses publicly commissions Joshua before the whole nation, giving him the same charge. Joshua will lead them to inherit the land.

f.w: in the sight of all Israel

n: The Lord goes ahead of Joshua. Courage comes from God’s presence, not from our own strength.
Moses wrote down the law and entrusted it to the priests and elders. Written scripture preserves God’s word after prophets pass on.
Every seven years, during the Feast of Tabernacles in the year debts were released, the law was to be read publicly.
When all Israel gathered at the sanctuary, the law was to be read aloud to everyone.

f.w: thou shalt read this law before all Israel

n: Everyone must come: men, women, children, and foreigners. God’s word is for all, and hearing leads to learning, reverence, and obedience.
Especially for children who had not yet learned — each new generation needs to hear the covenant for itself.

f.w: their children, which have not known any thing

n: The Lord tells Moses his death is near and summons him with Joshua to the tabernacle for Joshua’s commission.

f.g: The tent of meeting, where God met with Moses.

n: The Lord appeared in a pillar of cloud at the tent’s entrance, as he had throughout the wilderness.
A heartbreaking prophecy: after Moses dies, Israel will be unfaithful, chasing Canaanite gods. Idolatry is described as spiritual adultery.

f.w: thou shalt sleep with thy fathers

f.g: A metaphor for covenant unfaithfulness, like a spouse betraying a marriage.

n: God would hide his face — withdraw his protective presence — and troubles would come. Then they would realize: “God isn’t with us.”

f.w: I will hide my face from them

n: The hiding of God’s face would be the direct result of their turning to other gods.

f.w: I will surely hide my face

n: God commands Moses to write a song and teach it to Israel. Songs stick in memory long after sermons fade; this one would testify against them when they strayed.

f.g: The Song of Moses in Deuteronomy 32.

n: Prosperity would lead to complacency — eating, getting fat, and turning away. A pattern repeated throughout scripture.
The song would live on in their children’s mouths as a witness. God knew their inclinations even now.

f.g: I know their inclinations and intentions.

n: Moses wrote the song that very day and taught it to the people.

f.w: wrote this song the same day

n: The Lord himself now commissions Joshua with the same words: be strong and courageous; I will be with you.
Moses finished writing the law in a book.
He gave instructions to the Levites who carried the ark.
The book was placed beside the ark, which held the stone tablets, as a lasting witness to the covenant.

f.w: put it in the side of the ark

n: Moses speaks frankly: they had rebelled even while he lived; how much more after he is gone?
He calls the leaders together and summons heaven and earth as witnesses.

f.w: call heaven and earth to record

n: Moses foresees great corruption and disaster “in the latter days.” Prophets often warned of apostasy and later restoration.
Moses recites the entire song to the assembled people, introducing chapter 32.

f.w: in the ears of all the congregation
